title: Royal Ontario Museum
geometryBasis: The named 58-vertex museum envelope and mapped parts distinguish both stone wings, their roofs and links, and the nine sloped subvolumes that express the five interlocking Crystal forms. The archived named McLaughlin Planetarium footprint controls its separate podium.
sectionBasis: Per-part mapped heights, minimum heights and slope bearings establish the Crystal and stone massing. The Bloor photo establishes the open joint geometry, metallic cladding and diagonal blue glazing. The planetarium photo and period technical notes establish the visible dome and its 75-foot interior diameter.
limitations: The model depicts the 2015 museum complex, including the former planetarium. It predates later plaza changes and demolition of the planetarium.
The mapped outlines, heights and roof bearings control the masses. Some cantilever angles, glazed facet seams, fenestration and unphotographed elevations are estimates.
The original terrain remains unchanged. The building and pavement contacts use approximate local elevations.
